issues.title: Bitpacking select: produce flat compacted vectors for filtered scans
issues.hypothesis: In q01 the l_shipdate filter keeps about 98% of rows, but nearly every 2048-row vector loses a few. In RowGroup::Scan (src/storage/table/row_group.cpp:809-819), every non-filter column then goes through StandardColumnData::Select. Bitpacking (all 4 decimal columns: l_quantity, l_extendedprice, l_discount, l_tax) has no `select` callback; only constant, RLE and dict_fsst have one. So it falls back to ColumnData::Select, which scans the full vector and calls result.Slice(sel), so every payload column reaches the projections and the aggregate as a DICTIONARY vector. Downstream, the decimal multiplies and the aggregate scatter then take the generic sel-indirected paths instead of the flat ones. Measured with dbe-tool sql: Q1 with the filter is about 680ms. Without the filter, still scanning l_shipdate through an added max(l_shipdate), it is about 555ms, even though that version processes 2% more rows and runs an extra aggregate. Without the filter and without max it is about 480ms. So the filtered path costs at least about 18%, part of it from dictionary-sliced vectors.
issues.plan: In src/storage/compression/bitpacking.cpp add `template <class T> void BitpackingSelect(ColumnSegment &segment, ColumnScanState &state, idx_t vector_count, Vector &result, const SelectionVector &sel, idx_t sel_count)`, matching compression_select_t in compression_function.hpp:182. It decompresses vector_count values with the existing BitpackingScanPartial<T> logic into a per-scan-state scratch buffer of STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE T values. Add that buffer to BitpackingScanState<T> and allocate it lazily. It then gathers result_data[i] = scratch[sel.get_index(i)] for i < sel_count and leaves result as FLAT_VECTOR. Use a scratch buffer, not in-place compaction, so correctness never depends on the sel being sorted. Simplest route: call BitpackingScanPartial into a temporary Vector that wraps the scratch buffer (FlatVector::SetData), or refactor the partial scan to take a T* target. In GetBitpackingFunction set `bitpacking.select = BitpackingSelect<T>;`, keeping the ctor args unchanged, as done for get_segment_info. StandardColumnData::Select (standard_column_data.cpp:103) already routes through SelectVector when compression->select, the validity select and SCAN_ENTIRE_VECTOR are all present. Check that the validity segments of these columns (constant or uncompressed validity) have select callbacks: ConstantSelectValidity and ValiditySelect both exist. Also check that ColumnData::SelectVector's offset bookkeeping (offset_in_column += target_count) matches the bitpacking scan-state advance, which happens inside the partial scan by vector_count. Run the test/sql/storage compression tests for bitpacking.
issues.expected_gain: q01 5-12%: projections and the perfect-hash aggregate get flat inputs. The scan pays one gather of about 2000 values per column per vector instead of creating a dictionary slice.
issues.generality: Any filtered table scan over bitpacked integer, decimal or date columns (the default compression for most numeric data) where non-filter columns are projected, which is very common in TPC-H/DS-like workloads. Very selective filters pay a negligible gather of sel_count values. The full vector is still decompressed, as today.
issues.risk: Low-medium. This is a storage-layer change, so correctness is the main risk: DELTA_FOR state continuity (current_delta_offset must advance over all vector_count rows, not sel_count), CONSTANT mode, hugeint/uhugeint T, and segment boundaries. The SCAN_ENTIRE_VECTOR precondition guarantees the vector lies inside one segment.
